thread:
Maya Patel: Quick sync — finalizing launch comms and the webinar bench narrative. Need a short, repeatable framing we can hand to SDRs + a 2-line exec soundbite for the keynote. Also routing question: which landing page drives to demo vs benchmark signups?

Jon Rivera: Love it. My take: demo for enterprise / dedicated leads, benchmark signups for PLG/dev. Keep the exec soundbite focused on one promise: predictable economics + reliable latency.

Samir Khan: Agree on the split. For the benchmark story, can we lead with a single metric: 2–3x lower per-token cost at p95 latency vs cloud-managed endpoints? That’s sticky.

Elaine Cho: That metric is strong but we should avoid absolute numbers without a footnote. Suggest: "significantly lower unit costs while preserving p95 latency under load" and link to methodology in the appendix.

Maya Patel: Good call — add methodology link. Drafting two options for the 2-line exec:
```
Option A: Redwood Inference makes LLM-powered features predictable and economical at scale — same API, fewer surprises in latency and cost.
Option B: Ship LLM features faster with a production-first inference platform that controls latency and unit economics across environments.
```
Which lands better with field?

Jon Rivera: Option B. It highlights shipping speed (PLG) and production controls (enterprise).

Samir Khan: For SDR copy, we should give a quick battlecard line vs cloud AI platforms: "Cloud AI platforms sell scale; Redwood sells predictable inference economics and fallbacks — real-world uptime for customer-facing flows." Short + punchy.

Elaine Cho: Add a 1-sentence rebuttal for infra vendors (self-hosted runtimes): "Self-hosted gives control but costs ops time — Redwood pairs runtime performance with turnkey routing and observability so product teams move faster."

Maya Patel: OK. Routing: which landing page for webinar signups? Proposal: /launch/webinar-bench -> primary CTA "Get benchmark results" routes to benchmark signups; secondary CTA "Schedule a demo" routes to enterprise demo. That way SDRs get warm signal from demo clicks.

Jon Rivera: +1. Make demo CTA require company email to filter. Add UTM tags for "webinar-demo" and "webinar-bench".

Samir Khan: For the benchmark narrative slide, here's a micro-outline we can use in the deck (short bullets):
- Problem: unpredictable unit economics wreck feature velocity
- What we measured: p95 latency and cost-per-1k-tokens across workloads
- Result: caching + batching profiles reduced cost x while keeping p95 in-SLO
- Takeaway: pick the inference platform that optimizes for product SLAs, not just raw throughput

Elaine Cho: Love it. Can ops-bot post the tracking events we need for the landing page?

ops-bot: Event hooks created: webinar_bench_cta_click, webinar_demo_cta_click, webinar_signup_complete. Hooked to marketing-analytics pipeline. :robot_face:

Maya Patel: Perfect. Last asks: 1) snappy webinar title suggestions? 2) 3 quick QA bullets for SDRs to use in first-touch outreach.

Jon Rivera: Title: "Serving Real-World LLMs: Benchmarks, Routing, and Cost Controls"

Samir Khan: SDR QA bullets (short):
- When should I push a demo? -> If the buyer is enterprise/infra-focused or asks about SLA/region isolation.
- What’s the bench claim? -> We optimize unit economics while preserving p95 latency — methodology linked.
- Objection: "We can self-host." -> Net: self-host needs ops; Redwood gives running runtime + rollout and routing controls.

Elaine Cho: I'll turn these into a one-pager and add the methodology note. Maya, want me to draft the SDR Slack snippet?

Maya Patel: Yes please. If you can drop it by EOD we'll freeze messaging for the webinar comms. Thanks everyone :rocket:

ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: freeze-messaging workflow will send a 24-hour pre-freeze reminder at 1736590721.
